summary: Multi-segment timer with callbacks for cue-based sequencing, countdowns, and timed events. Outputs normalized fraction, elapsed time, and segment info.
key_concepts: Timer CHOP is an engine for running timed processes and emits fractions, counters, pulses, and timer-state channels.
Timers can be started by pulsing parameters or driving the input CHOPs, then counted in seconds, frames, or samples.
Python callbacks fire on timing events, allowing timed cues, playlists, timelines, state machines, and parameter or storage updates.
A single Timer CHOP can run multiple segments from a Table DAT, either serially or in parallel.
It can lock deterministically to the timeline or run sequentially with play/pause, speed control, cycle, break, and go-to behavior.
Info DAT and `.timecode` members expose segment timecodes and custom text while the CHOP outputs running/done/counter channels.

key_params.name: active
key_params.note: Cook never, always, while running, or while timeline is playing

key_params.name: timecontrol
key_params.note: Locked timeline, sequential, CHOP, or timecode master

key_params.name: length
key_params.note: Duration of the timer segment (in seconds or frames depending on units)

key_params.name: start
key_params.note: Start the timer and initialize if needed

key_params.name: initialize
key_params.note: Pulse to reset the timer to the beginning

key_params.name: ondone
key_params.note: Done action such as do nothing, reinitialize, restart, or restart without initialize

key_params.name: callbacks
key_params.note: Path to a DAT containing onDone, onSegmentEnter callbacks

key_params.name: cycle
key_params.note: Loop the timer when it reaches the end

key_params.name: subrange
key_params.note: Limit timer output to a subrange

common_gotchas: Start begins counting and initializes when needed; Play is a play/pause control rather than the only way to start the timer.
Callback DATs must define the correct function signatures or they will be silently ignored.
The first frame after Start can advance counters immediately; use Run Value style settings when a visible first frame must stay at zero.
